LLM-assisted Deep Reinforcement Learning for
Satellite Range Scheduling
Ke Li∗, Mingying Yang∗, Jing Li†, Bo Peng∗, and Xumin Yu‡
∗Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, 611756, China
†City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China
‡China Academy of Space Technology, China
Abstract—Satellite networks have emerged as a critical in-
frastructure in communication systems, providing wide coverage
and global connectivity. However, the growing scale and cross-
domain nature of the satellite range scheduling (SRS) problem
make efficient satellite and ground station resources scheduling
ever more challenging, especially for emergency tasks. Conven-
tional scheduling based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL)
suffers from sparse rewards in dynamic cross-domain satellite
network, limiting both training speed and solution quality. In
this study, we propose RAPPO, a Retrieval-Augmented Proximal
Policy Optimization framework that leverages retrieval-augmented
generation (RAG) to feed external SRS knowledge into a large
language model (LLM) for iterative reward function generation.
RAPPO comprises two modules: (1) LLM prompt initialization,
which retrieves knowledge of SRS via RAG; and (2) reward
function optimization, where the LLM generates and continuously
optimizes the DRL reward function based on scene descriptions
and reward-shaping knowledge retrieved during optimization.
In simulation experiments, RAPPO achieves an approximate
48.23% improvement in convergence speed, with load-balance
and transmission timeliness enhanced by about 30.83% and
31.04%, respectively, compared to conventional PPO. These results
demonstrate that integrating RAG-enhanced LLM reasoning into
reward design substantially improves DRL training efficiency and
scheduling effectiveness for cross-domain SRS.
Index Terms—satellite range scheduling, deep reinforcement
learning,

I. INTRODUCTION
With the widespread application of satellites in navigation,
weather forecasting, earth observation, disaster relief, as well
as military and civil scientific applications [1], [2], efficient
and intelligent scheduling has become essential. Especially
with the increasing frequency of natural disasters and military
conflicts, rapid emergency satellite response has become a
routine requirement, and the high demand for timeliness has
increased the complexity of scheduling. Satellite range schedul-
ing (SRS) problem [3] refers to the management of satellite
and ground station resources to satisfy the satellites’ commu-
nication requests, and it has emerged as a critical research

focus in response to the increasing complexity and urgency
of satellite communication. Moreover, to alleviate the shortage
of time-window resources caused by the surge in satellite-
ground communication tasks, cross-domain SRS is playing
an increasingly vital role. However, the complex constraints
inherent in cross-domain scenarios significantly increase the
difficulty of obtaining feasible and effective solutions.
An optimization model based on mixed-integer linear pro-
gramming has been proposed to assign tasks and communi-
cation time windows with ground stations for each satellite,
aiming to maximize satellite utilization [4]. However, the algo-
rithm used to solve this model is primarily designed for static
scenarios and struggles to find an optimal solution in dynamic
environments. A finite Markov decision process incorporating
heuristic algorithm has been proposed to optimize schedul-
ing performance, adopting deep reinforcement learning (DRL)
to solve the SRS problem in dynamic network environment
and enabling quick adjustments to schedules in response to
new requests or changes in satellite availability [5]. However,
these algorithms overlook the potential of communication links
across different satellite domains and struggle to ensure task
timeliness in scenarios with a high volume of urgent tasks.
A hierarchical sparse resource representation scheme has been
proposed to more effectively characterize the dynamic states
of cross-domain resources in satellite networks, and multi-
agent reinforcement learning is used to coordinate data trans-
mission strategies between satellites in different domains [6].
Although these works have achieved certain results in the
SRS problem, they still ignore the timeliness of satellite tasks
and the load-balance of data transmission resources in cross-
domain scenarios. Moreover, The cross-domain SRS problem
involves multiple constraints, such as ground station availability
and communication windows. These constraints increase the
difficulty for the DRL agent, which has a high demand for
reward signals, to achieve successful data transmission. As a
result, data transmission may encounter the problem of sparse
rewards [7], which significantly hinders the efficiency of agent
training.
As for the problem of sparse rewards in DRL, reward shaping
can be applied to adjust the reward signal [8], offering addi-
tional feedback to facilitate faster learning. This is particularly
important as the effectiveness of policy learning is closely
influenced by how the reward function is constructed. Reward

shaping relies on hand-crafted reward functions, but reward
functions are difficult to design [9]. In the cross-domain SRS
problem with a large number of urgent tasks, both timeliness
and load-balance need to be considered, further increasing the
difficulty of designing the reward function of DRL.
In light of the above insights, we propose a retrieval-
augmented proximal policy optimization by reward function
generation (RAPPO) framework with optimization objectives
of data transmission timeliness and load-balance of data trans-
mission resources to accelerate the training of DRL agents in
cross-domain SRS problem. This framework contains two mod-
ules. The first module is large language model (LLM) prompt
initialization, which aims to retrieve the knowledge relate to
SRS and reward shaping in the external knowledge base through
retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and input it to LLM as
part of the prompt. In the second module, LLM generates the
reward function of DRL using task description and external
knowledge, and iteratively optimizes it. The contributions of
this work are as follows:
• This paper investigates the critical challenge of ensuring
timely data transmission while achieving efficient load bal-
ancing across multiple domains within the cross-domain
SRS problem.
• To address this challenge, we introduce an approach based
on DRL, in which the reward function is dynamically
designed and iteratively optimized through the reasoning
capabilities of LLM.
• Furthermore, by leveraging RAG to incorporate external
knowledge from relevant knowledge bases into the LLM
input, we enhance the model’s ability to generate more
precise and contextually aware reward functions, thereby
improving the overall performance and adaptability of the
proposed approach.
II. SYSTEM MODEL AND PROBLEM STATEMENT

The set of all satellites is denoted by SA. gsg represents the

where k ∈1, 2, 3.

III. RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED PROXIMAL POLICY
OPTIMIZATION BY REWARD FUNCTION GENERATION
In this section, we will elaborate on each part of the proposed
RAPPO framework. The core of RAPPO is to utilize RAG
to obtain the correlation between the reward function design
task and external knowledge in the satellite scenario, and then
provide the LLM with available knowledge, enhance the ability
of LLM to generate reward functions. The proposed RAPPO is
shown in Fig. 2. The designing of the reward function can be
divided into two parts: LLM prompt initialization and reward
function optimization.
Fig. 2: The process of RAPPO.
A. Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization

scheduling decision variables at each time slot t. We can
convert this optimization problem in (13) to a sequential
decision-making problem and use the multi-agent proximal

problem. MAPPO in cross-domain satellite network refers to
learning problem in which multiple satellites can learn decision
policy at the same time. Each satellite can only gather local
observations from the environment, so a partially observable
Markov decision process (POMDP) model with state space and
action space is initially developed.

B. Retrieval-Augmented Reward Function Generation
In order to alleviate the problem of sparse rewards while
considering timeliness and load-balance, the reward function
for the SRS problem is shaped by LLM. Thus we introduce
the proposed RAPPO framework, which mainly consists of
two parts: LLM prompt initialization and reward function
optimization.
1) LLM Prompt Initialization: We first use the environment
code and task description as the initial prompts of LLM. In
order to enhance LLM’s understanding of SRS scenario, RAG is
used to expand LLM’s knowledge on satellite range scheduling
problem. Specifically, generalized scheduling model knowledge
for SRS problem is compiled, and the general method of DRL
reward shaping is considered to construct an external knowledge
base covering SRS problem and DRL reward shaping. Subse-
quently, the knowledge base is split into text chunks. And then
the embedding model (CodeBERT) [14] is used to vectorize
the text chunks and initial prompts. Finally, after calculating
the similarity between the text chunks of initial prompts and
the text chunks of external knowledge, the top-k most relevant

2) Reward Function Optimization: LLM (GPT-4o) designs
DRL reward functions based on user prompts and relevant

the generated string containing the DRL reward function is
parsed into executable reward function code and added to the
environment code for training the DRL agent. After the training
is completed, the performance of the agent is evaluated based
on the training data, and the training data is used as prompts
to further optimize the reward function designed by LLM. This
iterative process gradually improve the quality of the reward
function and the decision-making performance of the DRL
agent.
IV. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
We conduct comprehensive simulation experiments to eval-
uate the performance of MAPPO in satellite network. Firstly,
the experimental setup is introduced. Then, we compare the
performance results of MAPPO with three baselines.
A. Experiment Setup and Baselines
The experiments have been conducted in Python-3.8 with
Pytorch-based DRL framework. And we use STK-11.2 to
simulate the task scheduling scenario with 15 Chinese satellites
and 4 ground stations. The transmission rates of ISLs, IDLs
and SGLs are 80Mbps and 60Mbps respectively, and the
transmission bandwidth of SGLs is 80MHz. The scheduling
period is 24 hours.
In the proposed framework, the number of reward functions
generated by the LLM per iteration is set to 8, with 5 opti-
mization iterations performed. Furthermore, the actor network
learning rate of PPO algorithm is specified as 10−4, the critic
network learning rate is configured as 10−3, and the discount
factor is set to 0.99.
We introduce three baselines to verify the superiority of our
proposed framework, including one traditional DRL algorithm
and two reward shaping algorithms, which are respectively
given by
• PPO [13]: It optimizes the policy network by clipping
the probability ratio of actions, preventing the policy
from updating too drastically and ensuring the stability of
training. As a comparison algorithm, PPO adopts humans’
reward function without reward shaping.
• PPO-Lya [15]: It is based on the PPO algorithm, but
differs in that it shapes the reward function using Lyapunov
function to accelerate the training speed of DRL agent.
• LLM-PPO [16]: It also shapes the reward function of the
PPO algorithm. Unlike PPO Lya, the LLM-PPO algorithm
utilizes LLM’s understanding and reasoning abilities to
design the reward function.
B. Results
1) Convergence Evaluation: Fig. 3 evaluates the conver-
gence of RAPPO and comparison schemes. The convergence
speed of DRL training process reflects the ability of reward
function to deal with sparse rewards problem. We can obviously
see that the load-balance and timeliness of all algorithms gradu-
ally converge as the training progresses, and RAPPO converges
the fastest. Such a tendency greatly validates the effectiveness of
RAPPO in designing reward functions, indicating that LLM can
effectively understand complex SRS problem. The comparison
with LLM-PPO also indicates that RAG plays a significant role
in the scenario understanding of LLM.

V. CONCLUSION
In this paper, the satellite selection and task execution time
determination of data transmission tasks in cross-domain satel-
lite networks are studied. In order to improve the timeliness and
load-balance of data transmission resources, a reward function
design framework is proposed, which provides general satellite
modeling knowledge through RAG and designs competitive
reward function through LLM’s understanding of the scenario.
For future work, we plan to explore other multi-agent DRL
algorithms, as well as methods for handling sparse rewards, to
solve cross-domain SRS problems.
